summary.outcome: All 8 plans executed (60-08 Task 2 paused at human-action checkpoint). Ship-phase gates caught and fixed a real regression (60-05 broke the IPNS publish→resolve round-trip) and 7 in-scope CodeRabbit findings. repo: For Ed25519 IPNS records, `pubKey` lives in the IPNS name (k51…), NOT in the record protobuf bytes. `parseIpnsRecordBytes` does not yield `pubKey`; it must be supplied from the `publicKey` DB column (enforced at publish time via `deriveIpnsName(publicKey) === ipnsName`).

`decode_ipns_cbor_validity` in crates/core/src/ipns.rs used first-wins early-return for duplicate Validity keys, unlike its sibling `decode_ipns_cbor_data` which explicitly rejects duplicates — a parser-differential attack surface that D-07 intended to close.

`register_device` in crates/sdk/src/registry.rs had `Err(_) => None` swallowing ALL fetch errors including verification failures, triggering first-device bootstrap and auto-authorization on tampered/invalid IPNS records.

`parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs` in crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs silently accepted trailing date/time components and impossible dates (e.g., 2026-02-31) that Hinnant civil_from_days rolls forward into a LATER expiry — a fail-open gap at the D-07 EOL boundary.

`cargo fmt --check` reports workspace-wide drift on this machine due to a local rustfmt version mismatch vs. committed code style; never run `cargo fmt` without isolating to changed files — prior phase commits landed fine without it.
lint-staged only runs on TS/JSON/MD files, not `.rs` — Rust commits land with hand-written style as-is.
The GSD executor sometimes doesn't commit Cargo.lock after Cargo.toml edits that add new deps (60-01 added ciborium + cipherbox-core to api-client but left Cargo.lock dirty).
GSD executor ROADMAP checkbox updates are not always reliable — 60-06 ROADMAP checkbox was left unchecked despite a complete SUMMARY + passing tests.
Phase 60-08's Task 2 (staging DB wipe + redeploy + smoke-test) requires human action: staging VPS ssh access + real Web3Auth login — cannot be automated.
SDK E2E suite generates unique accounts per run (`email = ...-${Date.now()}@example.com`) so stale-DB collision is not a failure cause; a failing suite means a real regression.

code.finding: 60-05 removed `withCachedPublicKey` and the equal-seq signed-record enrich on a false assumption ('pubKey is already embedded in the signed record'). For Ed25519 records it is not — removing these caused resolveRecord to return records with no signature fields, breaking every publish→resolve round-trip in the SDK E2E suite (28/89 failures).

TS resolve path skipped the entire EOL block when Validity was not a Uint8Array — silently accepting records with no Validity field. Rust counterpart (crates/api-client/src/ipns.rs:114-117) fail-closes via `.ok_or_else(...)`. Fixed by mirroring the Rust contract: throw if Validity is absent.

decode_ipns_cbor_validity used early-return on first Validity key (first-wins); its sibling decode_ipns_cbor_data explicitly rejects duplicate Sequence/Value keys with a test documenting the parser-differential attack guard. Validity needed the same duplicate-rejection treatment.

register_device catch-all `Err(_) => None` bootstrapped a fresh authorized device on ANY error including VerifyError::Invalid. The only legitimate bootstrap signal is HTTP 404 (ApiError::IpnsNotFound). Fixed to propagate all other errors fail-closed.

parse_rfc3339_to_unix_secs accepted trailing date components ('2026-01-01-99') and impossible dates (2026-02-31, non-leap 2025-02-29) that Hinnant civil_from_days silently rolls into the following month, yielding a LATER expiry. This is fail-open at the D-07 EOL boundary.
Verify cache had no eviction bound — a sustained publish flood could grow it unboundedly. Fixed with an LRU-style size cap.
vault-settings sequence-fallback caught all errors and treated them as 'no existing record', bootstrapping fresh on verification failures. Fixed to propagate non-404 errors fail-closed.

workflow: The SDK E2E gate is the ONLY suite that exercises the real client→API IPNS publish→resolve round-trip — all unit suites (Rust 351, sdk-core 252, API jest 173) mock the boundary and would not have caught the 60-05 pubKey regression. Always run SDK E2E before shipping IPNS-touching phases.

Sequential gsd-executor subagents on the main working tree are preferable to worktree isolation for security-critical phases: worktree isolation has no reliable merge-back manifest, and sequential mode avoids parallel-write conflicts while keeping STATE/ROADMAP updates coherent.

The 1Password SSH signing agent can wedge after rapid commits (`op-ssh-sign: failed to fill whole buffer`); the agent still lists keys but signing fails. Recovery: quit and reopen 1Password desktop app (or toggle Settings → Developer → SSH agent off/on).
`gsd_run query commit` has a known false-negative — it reports `commit_failed` even when the commit lands. Always verify with `git log --oneline -1` before retrying or declaring failure.

CodeRabbit CLI local review (`coderabbit review --agent --base main --type committed`) before pushing is valuable: it found 7 real in-scope security gaps (duplicate-key parser, fail-open bootstrap, lenient RFC3339, unbounded cache, missing pubKey guard, web fail-open fallback, cache collision test) that all unit suites missed.

Running adversarial triage of review findings via a parallel workflow (15 agents, per-finding verify + patch) is the right pattern for security-critical phases — it separated 7 real fixes from 4 false-positives (including pre-increment-sequence checks that would have incorrectly rejected correct behavior) and 4 defer-todos without manual per-finding back-and-forth.

`git push` and `git fetch` are sandboxed and require explicit sandbox-disabled invocation, adding friction to every push/rebase step.
